text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.
LONDON - UK shares, still at the mercy of a volatile Wall Street, bounced back on Friday to recover just over half of Thursday's losses after a recovery in the U.S. market.

The FTSE 100 index closed 32.1 points higher at 4,089.5, but down 1.5 on the week. Trade remained relatively thin as many players kept well clear of the market. Gainers outweighed losers by about five times.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX share index ended bourse trade on Friday slightly higher, boosted by interest from German domestic fund managers and a strong performance from German Bunds. At the end of the session the DAX-30 index of German blue-chip shares stood at 2,859.28 points, up 10.51 points and up 6.4 on the week. In post-bourse trade the index rose 42.45 to 2,863.26.

PARIS - French stocks staged a partial rebound on Friday after investors were encouraged by higher bond prices and a rise on Wall Street, brokers said. The bourse also took heart from the appointments to the Bank of France's monetary policy council of two candidates viewed as more likely to favour lower interest rates, they said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which fell 2.54 percent on Thursday, recovered 25.79 points to close at 2,282.76. For the week, it was down 24.19 points.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended Friday's trading session mixed with blue chips mostly lower in overall quiet dealings. Dealers said softness in U.S. bonds earlier this week and subsequent interest rate worries weighed on Swiss financial shares, including banks and insurers. The broad Swiss Performance Index ended 0.16 points higher at 2,512.04 a gain of 10.96 on the week.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market was closed today for a
National Holiday. On Monday the Nikkei 225 index ended the final session of 1996 down 7.69 points at 19,361.35.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed slightly higher on Friday, holding steady above the strategic 13,200-point level despite renewed fears on Wall Street of a hike in U.S. interest rates, brokers said. "The market looks like it has stabilised," said Anthony Mak, associate director at Vickers Ballas. "But we could see it dip to 13,000 if there is further weakness on Wall Street." The Hang Seng Index closed 19.35 points higher at 13,222.79 a loss of 181.35 on the week.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed lower on Friday after a volatile Wall Street kept local investors nervous. The All Ordinaries index dipped 11.7 points to 2,399.5 a gain of 3.9 from last Friday's close. The market muddled about within a six-point range for all but the first 30 minutes of trade in the last day of the Christmas-New Year hiatus. Volumes remained subdued with many players still away.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares were hit by a sharp fall in the gold index on Friday as the price of bullion dipped worldwide, dealers said. At one stage gold in London fixed at $364.30 an ounce, below the psychologically important $365 level. The picture was a far cry from recent weeks when some analysts were eyeing a possible assault on $370 and sellers moved into the South African market. The gold index fell 30.1 points to 1,458 down 37.3 on the week and dragged the all-share index with it which finished the day down 19.4 points to 6,597.5 but up 14.4 since last Friday.

In industrials the performance was brighter as dealers took heart from better-than-expected M3 money supply figures released on Thursday. The industrial index gained 17 points to 7,876.5 and up 61.3 from a week ago amid a good mix of local institutional and overseas buying.
